description: Every table carrying a tenant_id column, its database isolation model, and its cross-tenant adversarial-proof status. tenant:isolation:check fails if a tenant-scoped table exists in the migrations but is absent here, or a registered table no longer exists — so a new tenant-owned table cannot ship unnoticed.

proofStates.pending: tenant_id enforced at the schema level, but no cross-tenant negative test proves A cannot reach B.
proofStates.proven: a negative test named in testReference proves cross-tenant read/write is rejected.

tables.isolationNote: The write boundary is real — the composite binding FK rejects a learning event for an unadmitted tenant — but production reads are not tenant-scoped: buildNotificationBrain (src/lib/phase5-achievement-engine.ts) and refreshLearningBrain (src/lib/learning-os.ts) aggregate learning_events WHERE student_id = $1 with no tenant/workspace predicate, and the legacy recordLearningEvent insert path sets no tenant columns at all. For a student admitted into two tenants, one tenant's reader would consume the other's learning evidence. Promotion is blocked on wiring a per-request tenant into the academy learning read/write paths, not on writing a test.

tables.isolationModel: tenant_id in unique constraint (tenant_id, event_type, event_id); enqueueNotificationDomainEvent inserts ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, event_type, event_id) and the conflict read-back filters WHERE tenant_id = $1
tables.isolationNote: The unique key and enqueueNotificationDomainEvent's conflict read-back are correctly tenant-scoped and load-bearing (an adversarial probe over a tenant-blind key rejects tenant B). But the sole production producer, enqueueAcademyAssessmentCompleted, calls resolveNotificationPrincipal without a request tenant, so principal.tenantId is pinned to DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_TENANT_ID and no production path ever supplies a second tenant. Cross-tenant behaviour is therefore unexercised through the real producer (same class as risk_authority_events). Promotion is blocked on threading a per-request tenant into the notification producer (#20), not on writing a test.

tables.isolationNote: Resolved: #310 un-pinned the risk domain — recordRiskDecision (and its siblings) now accept a per-call tenantId instead of hardcoding PLATFORM.DEFAULT_TENANT_ID. risk-enforcement-cross-tenant-isolation-postgres.test.ts drives two distinct tenants through the real authority, so cross-tenant behaviour is now exercised and proven, not merely schema-scoped.

tables.isolationModel: PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, principal_id) — one live enforcement row per (tenant, principal); tenant_id and principal_id are immutable and generation is a guarded column that must start at 1 and increment exactly once per update. Every durable decision and read is scoped WHERE tenant_id = $1, so the same principal active in two tenants owns independent enforcement rows and one tenant can neither read nor clear the other's live trading restriction

PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, principal_id, generation); every projection-debt row carries tenant_id and is forwarded by the internal publish path, and rows are append-preserved and DELETE-guarded, so tenant B's projection is published under tenant B and never collapses into or replays tenant A's

tables.isolationNote: The tenant_id column is dormant: the INSERT never sets it (it relies on the DEFAULT), the UNIQUE key is (withdrawal_id, generation) with no tenant_id, every read/update filters WHERE withdrawal_id/id, and the parent withdrawals table has no tenant_id column at all (only user_id). The whole withdrawal domain is effectively single-tenant today. A cross-tenant negative test cannot be written without fabricating multi-tenant behaviour the code does not implement. #109 for this domain first requires adding tenant_id to withdrawals and threading a real tenant through the external-effect authority.
